about.title: La Verne Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: La Verne's collisions cluster along a handful of predictable spots — Foothill Boulevard through the old downtown, the SR-210 on- and off-ramps, Arrow Highway near the rail crossing, and White Avenue where it feeds toward the university. Public records show 115 injury collisions and 155 injured people in the most recent year, with reports peaking Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., likely tied to school pickup and commuter traffic converging at once. Whether you were rear-ended waiting to turn onto Foothill or sideswiped merging off the 210, the aftermath is the same: medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster calling before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect La Verne residents with independent personal injury attorneys who handle these claims on contingency, so there's no upfront cost while you focus on getting better.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file suit, but if a government entity — like the City of La Verne or Caltrans on the 210 — is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can flag this early so you don't lose your claim before it starts.

items.title: Pure Comparative Fault Rewards Careful Documentation
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces your payout proportionally. That makes preserving evidence — dashcam footage, witness contacts, the police report — critical before memories fade or a busy intersection like Foothill and White gets repaved or restriped.

items.title: No Cap Means the Insurer Will Push Back Harder on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Because California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or emotional distress in most injury cases, insurers often try to minimize claims early with a recorded statement. Declining that call and letting an attorney handle communication protects your position.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally not a good idea before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to shift blame onto you, which matters a lot under California's comparative fault rules. A free consultation can help you understand what, if anything, you're required to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened near the SR-210 ramps and involved Caltrans property?
items.answer: Claims involving state or local government entities, including road design or maintenance issues near freeway ramps, come with much shorter filing deadlines — sometimes just six months. It's worth having an attorney review the location and circumstances quickly rather than waiting.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with one.
